title: Production Hyper-V Readiness, Resilience and Incident Capstone
summary: Integrate host readiness, failure-domain reasoning, virtual networking, evidence collection and senior operational judgement into a production Hyper-V assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit a business-critical Hyper-V estate where host readiness, network segmentation, maintenance headroom and incident evidence are inconsistently documented. Leadership requires a go/no-go operational-readiness decision before the next maintenance cycle.
business_context: The platform hosts mixed critical workloads and must tolerate planned maintenance without turning routine host work into a capacity or connectivity incident.
technical_constraints: Discovery begins read-only. Firmware changes, role installation, virtual-switch mutation, host reboot and workload migration require separately approved change authority.
functional_requirements: Produce host-readiness evidence covering virtualization capability, OS/version, resource headroom and supportability.
Map shared host, storage and virtual-network failure domains for representative workloads.
Reconcile virtual-switch/uplink/VLAN assumptions with approved network design.
Create an incident decision tree that separates host, hypervisor, network, storage and guest failure domains.
Define maintenance and failover acceptance criteria with measurable pre/post checks.
Present prioritized findings with owner, risk, validation and escalation boundary.
non_functional_requirements: No production mutation during evidence collection.
Conclusions must cite observable evidence, not only management-console health.
Recommendations must include rollback or escalation boundaries.
implementation_plan: Baseline host and workload evidence.
Map shared dependencies and capacity headroom.
Validate virtual-network assumptions.
Exercise a tabletop host/network incident using the documented decision tree.
Produce a prioritized readiness backlog and executive summary.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend a production-readiness decision with traceable host, network, capacity and failure-domain evidence plus bounded remediation actions.
rollback_dr: Any later state-changing remediation must have approved rollback and workload recovery boundaries; this capstone itself remains evidence-first.

assessment_rubric.failure_domain_reasoning: Separates shared platform faults from guest-only faults.
assessment_rubric.change_safety: Keeps mutation behind explicit approval and rollback gates.
assessment_rubric.operational_judgement: Prioritizes availability, supportability and maintenance headroom correctly.

title: Guarded Fabric Trust, Recovery and Security Assurance Capstone
summary: Integrate HGS trust architecture, attestation, key protection, evidence-first troubleshooting and disaster-recovery judgement into a guarded-fabric assurance exercise.
scenario: You inherit a guarded fabric protecting sensitive workloads. HGS service resilience, administrator separation, attestation evidence and recovery-key custody are only partially documented, and a controlled readiness review is required before platform change.
business_context: Protected workloads depend on HGS availability and trustworthy authorization decisions; weakening attestation for convenience would undermine the security objective of the platform.
technical_constraints: No attestation-mode switch, policy removal, key replacement, host authorization, unshielding or private-key export is allowed during assessment.
functional_requirements: Map HGS, guarded-host and shielded-VM trust boundaries and privileged-role separation.
Collect service, endpoint, attestation and certificate/key-custody evidence without changing policy.
Compare TPM-trusted and host-key assurance and document the selected operational model.
Build an evidence-first incident flow for host attestation or protected-VM startup failure.
Review backup/recovery custody for HGS state, policy and signing/encryption material.
Produce a recovery-readiness and security-risk backlog with explicit approval boundaries.
non_functional_requirements: Security controls are not weakened to obtain a passing health state.
Recovery conclusions distinguish service rebuild from preservation of authorization material.
implementation_plan: Baseline HGS service and trust configuration.
Review host-attestation evidence and privileged separation.
Review key/certificate custody and DR evidence.
Run a tabletop attestation/startup incident.
Produce prioritized security and recovery actions with ownership.
validation: Passes when the learner can explain and evidence the trust boundary, diagnose failure without bypassing policy, and produce a credible HGS recovery plan.
rollback_dr: Any trust-policy or key change remains a separately approved security change with tested rollback/recovery arrangements.

assessment_rubric.trust_reasoning: Correctly separates fabric administration from trust authority.
assessment_rubric.evidence_quality: Uses HGS/host diagnostics and policy evidence.
assessment_rubric.security_judgement: Rejects insecure shortcuts that weaken attestation.
assessment_rubric.recovery_readiness: Accounts for original authorization/key material and owner impact.

title: SCVMM Fabric Reconciliation, HA and Operations Capstone
summary: Integrate SCVMM architecture, compute-fabric onboarding, network/storage/library abstractions and evidence-first troubleshooting into a production fabric reconciliation exercise.
scenario: You inherit SCVMM managing production Hyper-V clusters. VMM inventory is mostly green, but logical-network, storage-classification and library ownership have drifted from the documented physical fabric.
business_context: Automation and placement are only trustworthy when VMM abstractions accurately represent the underlying compute, network and storage estate.
technical_constraints: Discovery is read-only. Host re-add, agent repair, provider refresh, credential changes, network/storage remapping, migration and deployment require separate approved change.
functional_requirements: Document VMM server, SQL and library availability/recovery dependencies.
Reconcile host groups, managed hosts and clusters against underlying Hyper-V/cluster truth.
Reconcile logical networks, VM networks, sites, VLAN/subnet mappings and host associations against approved network design.
Review storage classifications/providers and library shares for ownership, capacity and currency.
Build a decision tree that separates VMM management-plane faults from underlying fabric faults.
Produce a prioritized reconciliation and HA backlog with validation and rollback boundaries.
non_functional_requirements: Do not treat green VMM state as sole proof of fabric health.
No repair/refresh/remapping action is performed during evidence collection.
Every automation recommendation requires a reconciled source-of-truth assumption.
implementation_plan: Baseline VMM/SQL/library state.
Reconcile compute objects with Hyper-V/cluster evidence.
Reconcile network/storage/library abstractions.
Tabletop a management-plane versus fabric incident.
Produce HA, reconciliation and governance actions.
validation: Passes when the learner demonstrates that VMM abstractions match physical reality and can distinguish management-plane issues from underlying platform faults.
rollback_dr: All later VMM mutations require separate change, rollback and post-change reconciliation evidence.

assessment_rubric.fabric_reconciliation: Compares VMM abstractions with authoritative physical evidence.
assessment_rubric.layered_troubleshooting: Separates VMM from Hyper-V/cluster/network/storage failure domains.
assessment_rubric.ha_reasoning: Protects management server, database and library dependencies separately.
assessment_rubric.change_safety: Avoids repair actions until root cause and rollback are understood.

title: Production PowerShell Automation Safety and Reliability Capstone
summary: Integrate object-first design, remoting boundaries, error semantics, observability and safe-change engineering into a production automation review and redesign exercise.
scenario: You inherit an infrastructure automation script that works interactively but has inconsistent remote behavior, weak error handling, minimal evidence and unsafe retry semantics across a server fleet.
business_context: Automation must reduce toil without amplifying mistakes across many systems; reliability, evidence and bounded side effects are therefore first-class requirements.
technical_constraints: The assessment phase is read-only. Execution-policy changes, TrustedHosts changes, firewall/listener changes, privileged module installs and production mutation scripts require approved change authority.
functional_requirements: Refactor the design around object-first inputs/outputs and explicit function contracts.
Separate discovery, decision and mutation stages with a reviewable target set.
Classify remoting failures by DNS, transport, listener/firewall, authentication, authorization and endpoint policy.
Define terminating/non-terminating error handling and structured ErrorRecord evidence.
Define idempotence or safe-repeat behavior, preconditions, post-condition checks and correlation logging.
Produce a controlled rollout, rollback/compensation and test strategy.
non_functional_requirements: Secrets must not appear in source, logs or transcripts.
Read-only discovery must be independently testable.
Fleet automation must avoid blind blanket retries and uncontrolled partial success.
implementation_plan: Baseline current script behavior and failure classes.
Refactor object and function contracts.
Separate read-only discovery from mutation.
Design remoting/error/observability controls.
Define staged rollout, verification and compensation.
validation: Passes when the learner produces a reviewable automation design with structured evidence, bounded privilege, predictable failures and explicit post-condition verification.
rollback_dr: Any production mutation phase requires a defined rollback or compensation strategy and a bounded target set.

assessment_rubric.automation_design: Uses explicit inputs, object outputs and composable functions.
assessment_rubric.error_semantics: Handles terminating and non-terminating failures deliberately.
assessment_rubric.security: Preserves least privilege, secret hygiene and remoting controls.
assessment_rubric.operational_safety: Includes preconditions, post-validation, evidence and rollback/compensation.
